hints: Focus on what the white solid must be, since BaS2O6 is soluble but sulfate with Ba2+ is not.
Work out starting moles of BaS2O6.2H2O from 3.513 g and work out moles of BaSO4 from 0.661 g.
Link the two by the 1:1 decomposition, subtract reacted moles from starting moles, then divide by 0.100 dm3 to get concentration.
walkthrough:
**Identify the precipitate**

The starting salt is soluble, so Ba2+ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$ are in solution. In acid, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$ gives $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, which forms insoluble $\text{BaSO}_4$ with $\text{Ba}^{2+}$. So the 0.661 g white solid is $\text{BaSO}_4$.

$$\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{SO}_2(g) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq)$$
$$\text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s)$$

**Calculate initial moles of dithionate**

Use the hydrated $M_r$, including $2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. This is a very common trap.

$$M_r(\text{BaS}_2\text{O}_6\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 137.3 + 64.2 + 96.0 + 36.0 = 333.5$$
$$n_{initial} = \frac{3.513}{333.5} \approx 0.01053 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate moles that have decomposed**

One mole of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$ makes one mole of $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, which makes one mole of $\text{BaSO}_4$. So moles of precipitate equals moles decomposed.

$$M_r(\text{BaSO}_4) = 137.3 + 32.1 + 64.0 = 233.4$$
$$n(\text{BaSO}_4) = \frac{0.661}{233.4} \approx 0.00283 \text{ mol}$$

**Find remaining concentration**

Subtract to find moles of $\text{BaS}_2\text{O}_6$ still in solution, then divide by the flask volume in $\text{dm}^3$.

$$n_{remaining} = 0.01053 - 0.00283 = 0.00770 \text{ mol}$$
$$c = \frac{0.00770}{0.100} = 0.077 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$

options.A: This is the moles remaining, not the concentration. 0.01053 minus 0.00283 gives 0.00770 mol, but you must then divide by 0.100 dm3 to get 0.077 mol dm-3.
options.B: This comes from two slips together. If you forget the 2H2O and use Mr about 297.5 for anhydrous BaS2O6, initial moles become about 0.01181, minus 0.00283 gives 0.0090 mol. You then also forget to divide by volume.
options.C: Correct. Initial moles about 0.01053 minus decomposed moles about 0.00283 leaves about 0.00770 mol in 0.100 dm3, giving 0.077 mol dm-3.
options.D: This uses the anhydrous Mr. Forgetting the 2H2O gives initial moles 3.513/297.5 = 0.01181, minus 0.00283 = 0.00898 mol, divided by 0.1 gives about 0.090 mol dm-3. Always include water of crystallisation in the starting Mr.
